Alex / Monica — attaching the formal attestation and outlining the key operational controls below. Attachment: redwood_vm_attestation_letter.pdf

Summary (to paste into SIG/CAIQ fields):
- Scan cadence: authenticated internal scans weekly; unauthenticated external scans quarterly; dependency/third-party scanning run weekly for critical deps; authenticated infrastructure scans performed monthly.
- Retention: scan result artifacts (raw findings, scan exports) retained for 12 months; aggregated scan metrics retained for 36 months.
- CVE remediation SLAs (standard):
  • Critical (remote code execution / active exploit): 48 hours — emergency hotpatch + rollback plan.
  • High (privilege escalation, high-threat exposure): 7 days — patch-or-mitigate, with rollback tested in staging.
  • Medium: 30 days — prioritized by risk scoring and exposure.
  • Low: 90 days — tracked in backlog and included in quarterly maintenance waves.
- Exceptions / emergency process: we have a documented emergency patch workflow (exec escalation, immediate CI gating, hotpatch playbook, post-deploy verification).
- Verification & evidence: each closure includes: ticket id, PR/commit hash, deployment run id, post-scan evidence screenshot/export. These are indexed in the attached spreadsheet with links where appropriate.

Notes / caveats:
- For certain third-party components where upstream patching is required, we provide mitigation steps and timelines in the evidence index; we will flag those in your SIG packet.
- Our hotpatch SLA assumes customer-validated rollback windows where applicable for on-prem/private deployments — we’ll call that out per account.

Attached: redwood_vm_attestation_letter.pdf (signed by Trust lead) and the evidence index shared by Monica.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Trust & Security, Redwood Inference
